 New School Holidays in 2027: SB 1394 Establishes Farmworkers Day and AB 2017 Recognizes Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
 10.22.2026 On September 27, 2026, Governor Newsom signed Senate Bill (“SB”) 1394 and Assembly Bill (“AB”) 2017, making changes to California’s designated state holidays and the holidays that public school districts and community college districts may observe. [1] 
 SB 1394: Replacing Cesar Chavez Day With Farmworkers Day 
 Effective January 1, 2027, SB 1394 changes the designation of Cesar Chavez Day to Farmworkers Day and moves the recognized holiday from March 31 to April 10. SB 1394 amends Education Code sections 37220.5, 45203, 79020, and 88203, to reflect the new holiday designation.
 Per SB 1394, community colleges and public schools may close on April 10, known as Farmworkers Day, or the appropriate Monday or Friday preceding or following that date, if the governing board agrees to the closure pursuant to a memorandum of understanding with the exclusive bargaining representative. Similarly, the legislation authorizes classified employees of school districts and community college districts to receive a paid holiday for Farmworkers Day when agreed upon through the applicable collective bargaining process. The legislation does not independently require all public schools or community colleges to close on April 10.
 AB 2017: Recognizing Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha as State Holidays 
 Effective January 1, 2027, AB 2017 adds Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha to California’s list of designated state holidays and authorizes public schools and community colleges to recognize these holidays through their locally adopted calendars and applicable collective bargaining agreements.
 Per AB 2017, school districts and community college districts may elect to close schools or provide qualifying employees with paid holidays for Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, subject to the applicable statutory requirements and collective bargaining agreements. AB 2017 does not mandate that public schools or community colleges close for either holiday. Rather, the legislation provides additional flexibility for governing boards and exclusive bargaining representatives to negotiate the recognition of these holidays while considering local attendance patterns, staffing needs, instructional requirements, and other operational considerations.
 Should you have any questions regarding SB 1394, AB 2017, or the impact of these changes on school calendars, collective bargaining agreements, or employee holiday entitlements, please contact the authors of this Alert or your regular AALRR counsel.
 [1] Assembly Bill 1841 (2026) separately amends Government Code provisions concerning state holidays to address Native American Day (i.e., the fourth Friday in September). These amendments affect specified state employees, including teaching staff of schools under the jurisdiction of the State Department of Education or the Superintendent of Public Instruction. AB 1841’s provisions concerning Native American Day do not extend to public school districts, county offices of education, and community college districts. Under existing law, Native American Day remains a recognized holiday a governing board may elect to agree to a school closure pursuant to a memorandum of understanding.
